title: Teamleder for beredskab
description:
Teamleder til beredskab

Skab struktur, retning og handlekraft!

Vil du stå i spidsen for vores fysiske beredskabsarbejde og være med til at sikre, at Fjernvarme Fyn er godt rustet til at håndtere både kendte og uforudsete hændelser?

Vi søger en teamleder med faglig indsigt i fysisk beredskab, der vil stå i spidsen for et team på to medarbejdere. Du får en central rolle i at styrke vores beredskab i tæt samarbejde med vores cybersikkerhedsafdeling og resten af organisationen.

Du får en rolle tæt på både mennesker og drift, hvor du kombinerer ledelse med faglig opgaveløsning.

Hvem er vi?

Fjernvarme Fyn er en forsyningsvirksomhed med høj faglighed, stor fleksibilitet og en central rolle i den grønne omstilling. Vi arbejder målrettet med at udvikle og investere i fremtidens klimavenlige løsninger: vi vil skabe fremtidens klimaneutrale, robuste og konkurrencedygtige forsyning.
Det kalder på både fællesskab og handlekraft. Vores arbejdsopgaver spænder bredt, men uanset rolle og fagområde bidrager alle medarbejdere til samme mål: at skabe en mere bæredygtig fremtid.

Om jobbet
Din opgave er at omsætte beredskabets krav til arbejdsgange, der fungerer i hverdagen. Du arbejder selv med dokumentation, lovgivning og systemejerskab i relation til driften og sikrer sammen med teamet, at beredskabet løbende udvikles og vedligeholdes.

Du har en bred kontaktflade og samler den viden og de kompetencer, der skal til for at forbinde beredskabsarbejdet med den daglige drift. Som leder, hjælper du teamet med at prioritere og følge op, så der er klarhed over opgaverne og fremdrift i arbejdet.

Ansvarsområder
Du får derfor en spændende og varieret hverdag, hvor du blandt andet skal varetage:

  • Lede, prioritere og koordinere opgaverne i teamet samt sikre løbende opfølgning og fremdrift

  • Sikre struktur, dokumentation og efterlevelse af relevant lovgivning på beredskabsområdet

  • Koordinere indsatser og skabe sammenhæng med cybersikkerhedsafdelingen og resten af organisationen

  • Udvikle og vedligeholde processer, strukturer og arbejdsgange på beredskabsområdet i overensstemmelse med Fjernvarme Fyns forretningsstrategi

  • Samle viden og kompetencer og omsætte dem til konkrete prioriteringer og handlinger

Kvalifikationer
Kort om dig:

  • Har solid erfaring med beredskab og forståelse for relevante lovgivningsmæssige krav herunder Lov om styrket beredskab i energisektoren

  • Har erfaring med at skabe struktur, udvikle processer og sikre systematisk opfølgning

  • Kan omsætte komplekse problemstillinger til konkrete handlinger og prioriteringer

  • Har erfaring med ledelse eller et godt fundament for at varetage en ledelsesrolle – og lyst til selv at bidrage til opgaveløsningen

  • Kan skabe følgeskab, motivere og udvikle medarbejdere

  • Arbejder selvstændigt og tager ansvar, men samtidig formår at inddrage andre og skabe konsensus


Er du klar til at trække i arbejdstøjet sammen med os?
Så send os dit fyldestgørende CV sammen med en kort profiltekst. Det gør du ved at trykke på knappen ”Ansøg”. Vi ser frem til at høre fra dig senest d. 29/11.

Vil du vide mere om jobbet, så kontakt ansættende leder Majbrit Hoppe på mail: mho@fjernvarmefyn.dk med titlen ”Teamleder til beredskab”.

I ansættelsesprocessen vil vi gøre brug af Garudas kompetenceprofil og Fokusprofil.

Vi afholder samtaler på følgende datoer:

1. Samtale: 08/12
Garuda tilbagemelding 11/12
2. Samtale 15/12

Fjernvarme Fyn varetager en samfundskritisk infrastruktur, og derfor kræver stillingen en sikkerhedsgodkendelse. Det er med til at beskytte vores medarbejdere, driftskritiske funktioner og samfundets forsyningssikkerhed.

Du kan læse mere på PET's hjemmeside sikkerhedsgodkendelse.



Fjernvarme Fyn ejer de største kraftvarmeværker på Fyn, er Danmarks 3. største varmeforsyning og godt i gang med grøn omstilling henimod målet om klimaneutralitet.

title: Associate Software Engineer
description:
We are hiring an Assoc Software Engineer for the Telemetry Data Platform team, which carries product usage telemetry & performance telemetry for the entire ServiceNow platform on a stack built with Kubernetes, Kafka, and Click House. We are distributed across Israel, India, and the Americas.

This is a full stack role with its center of gravity firmly on telemetry development, data pipelines, Kubernetes and DevOps work, supporting Billions of records per day. You will be equally comfortable designing a distributed system and owning it in production. If you like following a system from the event that fires to the chart that renders — and you want the pager for it — you will feel at home.

You will lead design and delivery of complex, multi-service features, own technical decisions within a domain, and are fully self-directed — escalating only genuine ambiguities and driving decisions to closure. Of the ten critical skills at this level, incident response management is the only one set at Expert; the rest are Experienced.

What you get to do in this role:

  • Design, build, and own backend services for distributed data streaming and processing that handle high-volume, high-cardinality event data with predictable latency and no silent data loss.
  • Collaborate daily with a team of like-minded developers, product managers and quality engineers using agile software development methodology.
  • Master new areas and take ownership of features that matter to our customers.
  • Design features with a core commitment to quality and an eye to how the products will evolve in future releases.
  • Deploy, scale, and operate services in production Kubernetes environments, including Helm-based deployments and CI/CD pipelines that make releases repeatable and safe to roll back.
  • Own observability for what you build — meaningful metrics, useful logs, real tracing, and alerts that fire on customer impact rather than on noise.
  • Debug and resolve production incidents independently, participate in on-call, run root-cause analysis, and operate against defined service level objectives.
  • Work in a Scrum-based Agile development process that is light on documentation and meetings and heavy on coding

To be successful in this role you have:

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, software engineering, or a closely related – Required
  • Experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI’s potential impact on the function or industry
  • 2 years of work experience in software development
  • Experience with debugging and testing software through a CI lifecycle
  • Experience with Java, Python, OOP, and Design Patterns
  • Experience with relational databases such as MySQL and Oracle. Click house is advantage
  • Experience with Kubernetes in production, including Helm and CI/CD - Advantage
  • Some working knowledge and ability to use tools to assist with daily tasks (IDE, debugger, build tools, source control, ServiceNow instances, profilers, system administration/Unix tools)

title: .5 Life Skills Instructional Assistant
description:
Brookings-Harbor School District 17C

Brookings-Harbor High School
Life Skills Instructional Assistant
4 hours

PURPOSE: The Life Skills Aide assists the Teacher in the delivery of an instructional program. The Life Skills Aide prepares instructional materials, helps to maintain classroom discipline, and conducts planned activities using teacher-designated methods and materials with or without direct teacher supervision. The incumbent may also provide supervision of student activities in order to ensure that the school maintains a safe and orderly environment.

REPORTS TO: Principal, Vice Principal, Director of Special Programs

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:

  1. Conducts oneself in the best interest of students, in accordance with the highest traditions of public education and in support of the District's Mission.
  2. Assists in the academic instruction and presentation of instructional materials by individually working with small groups of students, or individual students:
    • reinforcing instruction.
    • following up on specific language, spelling, reading, mathematics, and other subject-area activities as directed by the Teacher.
    • monitoring and overseeing student tasks, practices and assignments in various subjects.
  3. Independently implements planned activities using Teacher-designated methods and materials for individuals and small groups for the purpose of instruction.
  4. Independently implements individual and group behavior plans.
  5. May be required to independently assist students in community-based activities offsite.
  6. Prepares and implements instructional materials using all available technology including augmentative communication devices and assistive technology devices.
  7. Provides physical accommodation to students who require it by:
    • assisting students in and out of mobility devices;
    • lifting students when needed;
    • assisting with orthopedic devices;
    • applying a specialized medical plan developed by a District Nurse or related specialist; and
    • providing assistance that may include toileting, lifting, pursuing or apprehending, restraining, secluding, providing physical prompts, and any other physical assistance needed for students within specialized programs for all disability types and cultural differences for ages 5 to 21.
  8. Encourages acceptable student behavior and assists in maintaining classroom discipline. Guides and reinforces student understanding of classroom rules and procedures. Supervises student interaction so that an orderly atmosphere is preserved. Controls aggressive behavior, settles disputes and otherwise encourages cooperative, well-mannered activity. Instructs as to acceptable and appropriate community behavior.
  9. Attends required trainings for certification in seizure protocols, mealtime plans, and tube feeding.
  10. Assists in guiding students to develop proper emotional control, physical hygiene, and discernment in judging and reacting to social situations; assures appropriate student behavior by coaching students during job performance, demonstrating tasks, monitoring attendance and implementing behavior support plans.
  11. May be required to ride school buses to support the needs of a student or students while they are being transported to or from school or a school activity. This may include arriving at a student's home pick-up location to serve as a support for the student on the bus and back.
  12. Confers with teachers concerning lesson plans and materials to meet student needs.
  13. Prepares, administers, and scores various tests and assignments as directed, including proficiency placement tests.
  14. Takes data on student performance while simultaneously instructing under the direction of the Teacher.
  15. Provides assistance to students as the students review and complete classroom assignments, homework, and projects.
  16. Assists students by answering questions, providing proper examples, and offering general guidance.
  17. Performs a variety of clerical duties using basic office equipment, computers, word processing software, spreadsheets, classroom software, and classroom computer programs:
    • Ordering, preparing, administering and correcting instructional materials.
    • generating computer documents and duplicating materials.
    • preparing lists and other documents, processing forms and applications,
    • maintaining student records and files as directed.
    • assembling materials, preparing individual profile charts, accounting for students.
    • compiling information and materials and preparing reports as requested.
  18. Works with accuracy and attention to detail to meet deadlines.
  19. Understands and executes oral and written instructions, policies, and procedures.
  20. Maintains confidentiality.
  21. Maintains effective working relationships with school personnel and students. Effectively works and communicates with students and staff from diverse cultures or backgrounds including those who speak limited or no English.

The statements contained above reflect general details as necessary to describe the principal functions of this job but should not be considered an all-inclusive listing of work requirements. Individuals may at times perform other duties as assigned which could include work in other functional areas to cover absences or relief, to equalize peak work periods or otherwise to balance the workload.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  1. Must possess or be able to obtain a valid Oregon driver's license.
  2. Must possess OIS certification or have completed other Restraint/Seclusion courses approved by the District within 90 days of hire.
  3. Must be able to drive to alternate locations in order to support students.
  4. Must have completed two years of post-secondary education or an Associate Degree, preferably including coursework in working with children in an educational setting.
  5. In lieu of Item 4 above, must possess both of the following:
    • High School Diploma or equivalent, and
    • Passing score on a qualifying state or local academic assessment that measures knowledge of and the ability to assist in instructing reading, writing, and mathematics. (In order to qualify, this assessment must meet the requirements of the federal Elementary and Secondary Education Act. Information about qualifying assessments is available in the Human Resources office.)
  6. Must have two years of previous training and/or experience in instructional techniques and behavior management and modification, preferably with disabled children and/or adults.
  7. Must be able to communicate effectively with other employees and students using tact, courtesy and good judgment.
  8. Must be able to collect data and perform basic mathematical functions.
  9. Must be able to communicate in written and spoken English with accuracy and attention to detail. Ability to understand and execute oral and written instructions.
  10. Must be able to operate standard office equipment such as computer, word processor, calculator and photocopier.


WORKING CONDITIONS:
The Life Skills Aide works largely within the classroom and other areas of the school building and grounds where students may congregate. Although the primary work is indoors, the Special Education Program Assistant frequently works outdoors supervising students, in variable weather conditions including inclement weather.

The incumbent must be able to stand and/or walk for long periods of time. The incumbent must be able to observe multiple students across large and small physical spaces and attend to individual student's needs while ensuring that other students are not unattended. The incumbent will need to walk quickly and run at times, and assume various physical postures associated with instruction and caring for students with special needs, including:

  1. Sitting;
  2. Running;
  3. Pushing and pulling;
  4. Toileting;
  5. Feeding;
  6. Restraining a student;
  7. Lifting up to 75 lbs;
  8. Bending, stooping, twisting, kneeling, reaching;
  9. Speaking and hearing often in a noisy environment.

Potential exposures include, but are not limited to: blood-borne pathogens; aggressive behavior from students; cold and hot temperatures; and inclement and severe weather. The environment includes working with students who have unique needs. Some students require significant physical assistance, others may demonstrate hostile and violent behaviors. Travel to multiple sites may be required. Occasional supervision of students or attendance at meetings or activities outside of the normal worksite may be required.

Work Year: 10 month
Employee Group: Classified BHEA Life Skills Aide
FLSA Status: Non-Exempt
Date Revised: May 4, 2015

title: Associate, Planning, UK
description:

4006 - Associate, Planning, UK

Role Summary and Impact

About WPP 650

Join an award-winning team at the heart of UK government, where your work will genuinely shape lives. As part of WPP 650 you’ll be part of a supportive, collaborative environment that values curiosity, kindness, and growth. Together, we use behaviour change principles to design smarter services, influence better decisions, and help millions of people across the country.

Named WPP 650, after the 650 UK constituencies, the name is a reminder that our work must reflect the full breadth of the country, every community, every audience. No two days are the same. The challenges are complex, the problems worth solving, and the learning constant. You’ll tackle issues that matter, alongside talented colleagues who care deeply about what they do. It’s demanding – but always rewarding.

WPP 650 is a bespoke agency unit within WPP, dedicated to serving the evolving communications needs of government clients. We bring together the best of WPP's talent, technology, and insights to deliver impactful, modern, and effective public communications. We are at the forefront of reimagining how government engages with its citizens.

This is meaningful work with real-world impact – the kind you can point to with pride.

About the role:

The planning team are the guardians of creating industry leading, unrivalled work at WPP 650. We are the central conduits to all specialists, striving to push boundaries and have a positive impact on consumers and brand.

WPP 650 is looking for a Planning Executive to join our growing planning team, to support the planning team and give your career a flying start in the media industry.

In this role, you will:

Media planning craft:

  • Develop a baseline of media planning knowledge across channels.
  • Learn and use media systems and tools including, but limited to, Open, TGI, Pathmatics, AdIntel, etc.
  • Run and analyse reports including audience insights, etc.
  • Need an inquisitive and curious mindset, wanting to understand and learn more about media planning.
  • Build your own knowledge by staying on top of the latest trends and news impacting the media industry.

Campaign management:

  • Learn the fundamentals of effective campaign management including updating schematics, providing media plans to clients, chasing creative, etc.
  • Assist with financial processes e.g. PO trackers, bookings, reconciliations, queries.
  • Work closely with activation teams to deliver responses and tactical plans.

description:
About the Department

Henry Ford Medical Center – Fairlane in Dearborn provides 24-hour emergency care in a fast-paced environment serving patients with a wide range of urgent and emergent needs.

This is a part-time, 24-hour day-shift position.

Our team is looking for professionals who are reliable, adaptable, collaborative, and strong communicators. Successful team members are able to prioritize quickly as patient needs change, take initiative, and work effectively as part of the emergency care team.

This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys hands-on patient care and thrives in a busy setting where teamwork, responsiveness, and excellent patient care are essential.

Role Overview

As an Emergency Room Technical Assistant, you will provide hands-on patient care and clinical support under the direct supervision of Registered Nurses and Providers. You will work alongside the emergency care team to support safe, timely, and efficient care throughout the department.

Position Details

  • Hours: 24 hours per week
  • Shift: Days
  • Employment Status: Part-time

Why Henry Ford Health

At Henry Ford Health, we are relentless advocates for exceptional care for our patients, communities, and each other. We come to do meaningful work and grow our careers, and we stay for the connection, support, and shared pride in making the impossible, possible.

  • Assist RNs and Providers with patient assessments, examinations, treatments, and procedures.

  • Prepare patients, equipment, and sterile supplies for procedures, including suturing, casting, pelvic exams, and lumbar punctures.
  • Recognize and promptly report abnormal vital signs or potentially life-threatening cardiac rhythms to the RN or Provider.
  • Document patient care and follow safety, infection prevention, and standard precaution requirements.
  • Support patient flow through patient transport, room turnover, equipment cleaning, and restocking.
  • Provide compassionate support to patients and families while contributing to an excellent patient experience.

    At Henry Ford Health, we offer opportunities for career growth, collaboration with leading healthcare professionals, and the chance to engage in mission-driven work. You'll have access to continuous learning and development, enabling you to make a meaningful impact in the lives of our patients and communities.

    Join Our Team

    Ready to make a difference? Apply now to join our dedicated team at Henry Ford Health!

    What You Will Need

    • High School diploma or GED equivalent.
    • BCLS certification.
    • One of the following certifications/programs:
      • B-EMT
      • Graduate from a formal Medical Assistant program
      • Completion of a formal nursing education program
      • Completion of a formal medical doctor education program
      • OR one (1) year of applicable Emergency Room Technical experience in lieu of the above completed certification/program. Must complete applicable certification/program within 12 months of hire.
    • Successful completion of a 180-day orientation period required.

    Preferred Qualifications

    • Previous Emergency Department Technician or Medical Assistant experience.
    • EMT license.

title: Community Director, EMEA
location: London, London, City of, United Kingdom
description:
Hybrid with 2 days per week in the office

About Greenpark

Greenpark is a global, award-winning digital agency specialising in omnichannel search and social. Our raison d’etre is to create amazing content that people and algorithms love. How? Through data-led and performance-driven search and social content to help brands create meaningful connections that impact people's lives. Our unique expertise in Omnichannel Search & Insights, Creative Content and Performance Tech are delivered to our clients via an ad agency and in-house models. We do this for a global client portfolio including Unilever, Campari Group, AIA, Sanofi, Nestle, Lipton, Kimberley Clark, Straumann, Ricola, Globe Telecom, and more.

Want the real inside scoop? Our Playbook gives you a peek into how we work, collaborate, and get things done at Greenpark. Check it out here

Our Values

As a company, we strive and act together in our ambition to make a positive impact for the people and brands we serve, we do everything with kindness and respect at the core. ‘We Strive’,
‘Acting Together’,
‘With Kindness’ are the values that guide us.

About the role

As Community Director, you’ll lead community strategy and management across a portfolio of our EMEA clients, spanning Greenpark’s verticals including food and drink, health and pharmaceuticals, beauty and wellness, and luxury. You’ll own how Greenpark does community – our ways of working, our team and our tools – and make sure every conversation builds trust, loyalty and performance for the brands we serve. This is a data-led role: social listening, community insight and robust reporting sit at the heart of it, showing the value of community and feeding what audiences say and search for into content, social search and wider search strategy. You’ll understand the growing role community conversations play in how brands are surfaced by AI assistants and LLMs, and champion smart, responsible AI integration across community workflows. You’ll lead and grow a team of community leads and managers, act as a senior client partner and help shape Greenpark’s community offering for new business, working closely with our Social, Search & Insights, Influencer, Digital PR and Performance Tech teams. You’ll report to our Social Media Director.

What you’ll do

  • Set and own community strategy for a portfolio of EMEA clients, defining how brands show up, engage and build loyalty across Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, YouTube, Reddit, LinkedIn and owned communities, aligned with Greenpark’s omnichannel search and social offering.
  • Define and govern Greenpark’s community management ways of working – playbooks, tone of voice, response frameworks, SLAs, moderation, escalation, and issues and crisis management – ensuring consistent, compliant, high-quality community management across accounts, including regulated categories.
  • Lead social listening and community insight across accounts, tracking sentiment, conversations, trends and the questions audiences are asking, and turning them into insight that shapes social, web, editorial and search strategy.
  • Own community reporting and measurement – setting KPIs such as response times, sentiment, engagement quality and community growth, and building dashboards and monthly reports that demonstrate the business value of community.
  • Use community and listening insight to drive social search and LLM visibility, informing content that is discovered in platform search and working with our Search & Insights team to understand how community conversations on platforms such as Reddit and YouTube influence how AI models surface and cite brands (GEO/AEO).
  • Lead AI integration across community workflows – from listening and triage to response drafting, moderation and reporting – with clear quality standards, human oversight and guardrails, and upskill the team to use AI tools well.
  • Build, lead and develop a high-performing team of community leads and managers, including resourcing, coverage models across time zones, tooling and training.
  • Act as a senior client partner and lead on new business, presenting strategy, performance and recommendations, pitching Greenpark’s community offering and evolving it alongside our Social, Influencer, Digital PR and Performance Tech teams.

About you

  • Significant experience (8+ years) in social media and community management, including senior agency experience leading community strategy and teams for brands across sectors such as food and drink, health and pharmaceuticals, beauty and wellness, and luxury.
  • Deep community management expertise, with a track record of building playbooks, escalation and crisis frameworks, and managing communities and issues at scale – including within regulated categories such as pharma.
  • Highly data-literate, with expert knowledge of community and social analytics, experience building dashboards (e.g. Looker Studio or Power BI), and the ability to turn data into clear insight that proves the value of community.
  • Hands-on experience with social listening and community management platforms (such as Brandwatch, Talkwalker, Sprout Social, Emplifi or Khoros), and experience setting up the tools and processes a team needs to perform.
  • A strong understanding of social search and how communities, comments and user-generated content help audiences discover brands and products on TikTok, Instagram, YouTube and Reddit.
  • A clear understanding of social and community’s role in LLM visibility (GEO/AEO) – how community conversations and content influence how brands are surfaced and cited in AI search – and a curiosity about where this is heading.
  • Practical experience integrating AI tools (such as Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and AI features within listening and community platforms) into community workflows; experience developing AI guidelines or governance is a strong advantage.
  • A proven people leader who builds and develops high-performing teams, with a collaborative, coaching style, and comfortable working within a global team across time zones.
  • A confident senior client partner, experienced in presenting to senior stakeholders and leading pitches and new business.
  • You live & breathe Greenpark’s core values ‘We Strive’, ‘Acting Together’, ‘With Kindness’ – championing openness, respect, innovation, and teamwork – so that every interaction, both internally and externally, reflects our commitment to our values.

At Greenpark, we believe the best ideas come from the widest range of perspectives. We welcome and celebrate every background, identity, and experience across our global workforce. By fostering a culture of respect, inclusivity, and collaboration, we’re committed to ensuring everyone’s voice is heard and everyone can thrive.

All applications shall be considered for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, neurodivergence, disability status or any other protected characteristics.

description:

Job Category: Information Technology

* * *


The Opportunity:

As the Advanced Cyber Analytics team lead, you will be tasked with developing and maintaining defensive countermeasures for the enterprise. Working within a Fusion model, you will collaborate with other teams within Focused Operations with the task of proactively preventing a successful compromise and eradicating persistent adversaries already in the enterprise. This will be done through various means such as reviewing future and past intelligence reports, reviewing incident reports, through regular Purple Teaming exercises, and continuously validating Defensive Countermeasures already deployed.


Responsibilities:

• Lead the Advanced Cyber Analytics Team in developing and maintaining countermeasures, integrating the team in Focused Operations and other outside teams’ processes, providing expertise to train/mentor more junior members.
• Analyzes trends and patterns of data on NGA networks to identify and predict previously undiscovered events and incidents and develop or tune rules/signatures/scripts as needed.
• Coordinates with Defensive Cyber Operations and Focused Operations to develop or tune rules/signatures/scripts.
• Coordinates with other Cybersecurity Operations Services to investigate and obtain information about potential sources of compromise on enterprise systems and develop or tune rules/signatures/scripts as needed.
• Correlates and analyzes precursors to incidents and develop or tune rules/signatures/scripts as needed.
• Will collaborate with the Cyber Data Analytics team to achieve SIEM alert efficiency though evaluation of valid alerts and false positives, and develop or tune rules/signatures/scripts as needed
• Work with the Cyber Incident Response Team by assessing ongoing incident activity to predict adversary responses and locations of compromise to assist with triage.
• Documents all work in the authorized ticketing system with a sufficient level of detail to ensure all stakeholders can systematically reconstruct the analysis.
• Provide input to reoccurring meetings and briefings as required.



Qualifications:

Required:

• Must be a US Citizen with an Active TS/SCI.
• 8+ years of related advanced cyber security analytics work experience.
• Must have a certification that is compliant with DoD 8140.01 and DoD 8570.01-M IAT Level III and CSSP Analyst.
• Experience with data mining or building queries in a SIEM.
• Strong understanding of signature development and tuning.
• Strong understanding of network protocols and analysis with protocol analyzers.
• Knowledge of static file signatures, i.e. "magic numbers" and how it applies to developing countermeasures for files in transit and that reside locally on a host.
• Good working knowledge of regular expressions.
• Excellent written and verbal communication


Desired:

• Comfortable in a hex editor.
• Ability to write python/bash/PowerShell scripts.
• Ability to analyze each use case, as it pertains to detection logic, and identify the corresponding capability.
• Good understanding of Purple Team Tactics.
• Familiarity with security in a cloud environment and how it applies to visibility gaps, data lakes and data mining.

-

A culture of integrity.

Together, we will advance our nation's most critical missions, build on our lengthy track record of business success, and find opportunities to break new ground — in your career and in our legacy.

title: Research Scientist, Discovery (Engineering & Applied Sciences)
location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

Research Scientist, Discovery (Engineering & Applied Sciences)

About the Team

Our team is organized around the north star goal of building an AI scientist – a system capable of solving the long term reasoning challenges and basic capabilities necessary to push the scientific and technological frontier.

About the role

On the Discovery team at Anthropic, we're expanding our work on engineering and the applied sciences. Our goal is to contribute to training Claude to invent, design, and engineer across every discipline and scale, reliably and safely: new manufacturing and experimental techniques, processes, materials, devices, instruments, machines, energy systems, and factories. We want this work to accelerate science and technology and benefit people widely.

To achieve these goals, we're seeking exceptional machine learning researchers with deep expertise in training and evaluating frontier models. In this role, you'll work end to end across the model stack, developing training environments, rewards, data, and evaluations that measure and improve Claude's performance on complex engineering and scientific tasks, and carrying what works into production training runs. You'll collaborate closely with researchers, engineers, and partners across Anthropic and industry to build AI systems that can engage in all phases of research and development, and that learn from real-world feedback. A background in engineering or the sciences is a plus but not required.

Key responsibilities

  • Design, build, and study reinforcement learning environments, rewards, and training data that improve Claude's capabilities in engineering and the applied sciences
  • Create benchmarks and evaluation frameworks that measure model performance on realistic engineering and scientific workflows
  • Develop simulation-based training environments and verifiers, working with domain experts to validate them against real-world data
  • Develop approaches to long-horizon task completion, multi-agent collaboration, and complex reasoning essential for real engineering and research work
  • Research how models can learn efficiently from experiments and real-world feedback.
  • Study how environments and rewards behave in large-scale training, including robustness, calibration, and generalization, so that training produces models that are both capable and well aligned
  • Scale research ideas from prototype to production training runs
  • Collaborate with domain experts and industry partners to build and test what Claude invents, designs, and engineers, and turn that feedback into training and evaluation signal
  • Help chart how Claude’s engineering capabilities reach real-world use: where they matter most, what stands in the way of adoption, and how that should shape research priorities

You may be a good fit if you have:

  • Proficiency in Python and hands-on experience with a modern machine learning framework such as PyTorch or JAX
  • Hands-on experience training or evaluating machine learning models
  • Track record of machine learning research: forming hypotheses, designing and running experiments, and drawing sound conclusions from the results
  • Ability to implement your own research ideas and diagnose problems in complex systems
  • Ability to learn unfamiliar technical fields quickly and work productively with experts in them
  • Clear communication and a collaborative approach to solving problems
  • Excitement about improving Claude’s scientific capabilities and the downstream impact on science and technology
  • Commitment to developing AI that is safe and beneficial

Strong candidates may also have:

  • Experience with reinforcement learning and pre-training on large language models, including environment and reward design
  • Familiarity with large-scale language model training, evaluation, and inference pipelines
  • Published research or practical experience in AI for science or engineering, or in long-horizon reasoning
  • A degree or work experience in an engineering or applied science discipline, such as mechanical, electrical, materials, chemical, aerospace, systems, or manufacturing engineering, applied physics, or computational simulation
  • Experience building simulators, surrogate models, or simulation-based environments and verifiers, and calibrating and validating them against real-world data
  • Experience with large-scale data pipelines and technical or multimodal datasets
  • Demonstrated ability to work across multiple domains, such as language modeling, systems engineering, and scientific computing

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$350,000—$500,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

title: Lead Recovery Advocate
description:

1. Responsible for the direct management and guidance of recovery Advocates
a. The Lead Recovery Advocate will provide direct supervision to the Recovery Advocate Staff, including interviewing/hiring, training and development.
b. Conduct annual performance appraisal for direct reports.
c. Assist with HRIS software module to manage staff timecards, and PTO requests.
d. Develop, maintain, and adjust staff coverage using census and organizational needs to help guide this process.
e. Liaison of information and/or changes in directives or initiatives as well as modeling those directives or changes.
f. Recognition of employee strengths, growth opportunities as well as managing disciplinary or performance issues through supervision, annual employee reviews, and in the moment opportunities.

2. Assist Administrative/Clinical staff with patient movement and clinical services, including departing and arriving patients, coordination of 12-Step Meeting/Lecture attendance, and taking patients to synagogue and/or other places of worship as required
3. Be present on unit and engaging with staff and patients.
4. Support the admission, transfer, and discharge process for the patient.
a. Perform luggage checks and transfer luggage weighing up to 50 pounds.
b. Conduct on person searches and document patient belongings.
c. Facilitate new patient orientation and unit tours.
5. Organize patient movement.
a. Help organize patients for off-campus appointments as required.
b. Ensure patient attendance to scheduled programming and accompany and/or monitor as required.
c. Accompany patients to meals and activities.
d. Assist with guest speakers and in-house recovery support meetings.
e. Monitor and direct patients during emergency evacuations.
6. Assist the clinical and admission teams to monitor and assess patient behavior (i.e.: eating disorders, psychiatric disorders, aggressive and self-injurious behaviors) with supervision/support of a clinical or administrative staff member.
a. Assist elopement, Against Medical Advice (AMA), and Against Staff Advice (ASA) protocols.
b. Maintain communication with clinical staff regarding patient issues.
c. Conduct and document hourly head counts of patients or their whereabouts.
d. Document patient behavior in electronic medical record.
e. De-escalate patients.
f. Perform daily room/perimeter checks and periodic room searches.
g. Educate patients with behavioral health disorders on the use of recovery-oriented stress management, social, relational, and coping skills to build and sustain recovery.
h. Conduct the Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS) when needed for indicated
i. Follow protocol for patients returning from off-site passes, including but not limited to observation of urine, drug screenings, breathalyzers, completion of on-person search and luggage search.
7. May present educational lectures with clinically approved materials.
8. Monitor and work with patients to ensure common areas are kept clean, neat, safe, and presentable.
9. Handle any patient concerns or emergencies with discretion and professionalism, ensuring prompt resolution and follow-up.
10. Proactively identifies and fulfills patient requests, providing solutions before they are asked for and maintains a high level of service throughout the patient's experience.
11. Schedule Spa services for patients, when applicable.
12. Responsible for internal and external running of errands (forgotten items, purchases, etc), when applicable.
13. Supports pet care services including boarding, medical appointments, grooming, etc., when applicable.
14. Handles deliveries and shipping of patient items, when applicable.
15. Collects dining preferences and assists with dining reservations for OD and PHP, when applicable.
16. Books local activities for OD and PHP patients, when applicable.
17. This job description reflects management’s assignment of essential functions; it does not restrict or prescribe other duties or tasks that may be required or assigned.


Physical Requirements:
The physical and mental demands described here are representative of those that must be met to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
1. Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds.
2. Must be able to walk and actively participate in activities throughout campus, which may include ascending and descending stairs.
3. Must be able to sit for prolonged periods of time as needed.
4. Must be able to drive a 15-passenger van, car, or car to and from various activities.
5. Must be able to work overtime/extended hours, holidays, and during periods of inclement weather as needed.
6. May include after-hours calls.


Education/ Experience/Qualifications:
1. High school diploma or equivalent is required.
2. Requires proficient computer skills, including knowledge of Microsoft Office
3. Minimum of 2 years working with substance use disorder patients
4. 2 years of experience in direct supervision of employees preferred.
5. Requires a basic understanding of substance use disorders and recovery program of philosophies.
6. Must be 21 years of age or older.
7. Must be compliant with applicable federal, state and local laws and clearances.
8. Requires a current, valid, unrestricted driver’s license with at least 3 years of driving experience for Florida employees and 5 years of driving experience for Pennsylvania employees.

title: Radio Firmware Engineer
description:
• Develop, test, and maintain the low-level firmware drivers that abstract a consistent, future-proof, and well-documented interface to the radio of Renesas wireless SoCs, throughout the complete IC development cycle.
  • Closely follow standardization efforts and translate existing and roadmap radio PHY requirements into highly efficient firmware solutions, in order to provide Renesas a competitive advantage in the IC market.
  • Contribute to shaping the future of Renesas wireless products.

Principal Accountabilities:

  • Implement, test, and maintain the radio low-level firmware drivers for wireless SoCs.
  • Fine-tune the firmware for optimal performance, energy efficiency, resource utilization, and reliability.
  • Contribute to the integration of the radio low-level drivers into wireless protocol stacks.
  • Develop and maintain radio low-level firmware for IC simulation, production test, lab evaluation, qualification, and characterization.
  • Implement and maintain automated regression tests for the radio firmware.
  • Troubleshoot firmware / software and architectural issues.
  • Create and maintain documentation and Application Notes.
  • Schedule own tasks, report progress to project leader, identify possible project issues.
  • Work closely across teams and contribute to datasheets, architectural spec’s and development plans for new designs.
  • Industry experience in Embedded Software for ARM or DSP cores.
  • Background in highly resource-constrained, real time, embedded environments.
  • Solid C and Python Language skills.
  • Experience with Assembly Language for at least one microcontroller family.
  • Experience with software engineering processes and the full software development lifecycle, including requirements, design, implementation, testing, and deployment.
  • Experience with version control systems, e.g. Git.
  • Proficiency with electronics bench test equipment, e.g. logic analysers, debug probes, oscilloscopes, spectrum analysers.
  • Proficiency in problem solving and debugging skills.
  • Eagerness to contribute new ideas, build consensus, and drive tasks to completion.
  • Desire and mental agility to quickly understand new ideas in novel domains.
  • Excellent team working skills, multi-disciplinary focus.
  • Talent for clearly communicating challenging technical subject matter.
  • Fluent in English language (written and oral).

Desirable

  • Knowledge / experience in any of the following fields is an advantage: low-level drivers, low power wireless protocol stacks (Bluetooth, Thread, Zigbee etc.), MAC and Physical Layer (PHY) techniques, Software Defined Radio techniques, Digital Communication Theory, DSP Theory, MATLAB.
  • Familiarity with embedded software tools such as GCC, GDB, Make, CMake etc.
  • Experience with chip development flow / commercialization.
  • Understanding of hardware vs. software trade-offs, and experience in specifying hardware requirements and working with hardware engineers.
  • Familiarity with hardware description languages.
  • Experience in Test Methodologies / Automation; familiarity with Wireless Communications test equipment.
  • Strong mathematical fundamentals.
  • Published scientific/technical articles or presented papers at technical conferences.

title: North West London - Job Pool
description:
WHY WORK AT JOE & THE JUICE

JOE & THE JUICE is a people-centric food and beverage company built around culture, not just juice, sandwiches, coffee, and much more. When joining us, you step into a high-energy community where the music is loud, the bar is your stage, and your personality matters as much as your skills.

We believe in four simple virtues that shape everything we do:

  • Positive Attitude
  • Inclusion
  • Social Ties
  • Growth

For us, this means that when you choose a cup-half-full mindset, welcome people from every background, build real friendships across the bar by creating great guest experiences, and use every shift as a chance to learn something new — you become more than just a Juicer; like us, you continue to search and find purpose and meaning in what you do.

From your first day, you’ll be part of an international network of Juicers who support each other, celebrate wins together, and push each other to grow. You will learn by doing, move through a clear Moneyball career path, and be part of a company where most leaders have earned their stripes behind the bar (fun fact: over 75% of our employees started as Juicers!).

If you love fast-paced service, music, people, and the idea of turning a job into a lifestyle, JOE can become a place to build skills, friendships, and a career that can take you across cities, countries, and roles.

THIS IS A TALENT POOL, NOT A JOB OPENING

We're not hiring for a specific store right now. By applying here, you're joining our Juicer talent pool, so you're first in line when a spot opens near you. If and when the right opportunity comes up, we'll reach out. No promises on timing, and no need to wait by the phone, but your application stays with us and we'll come back to you when there's a match.

STORES IN THIS POOL

This pool covers the stores below. When a Juicer position opens in any of them, you'll be among the first we reach out to.

  • 63 Hampstead High Street
  • Chalk Farm
  • 205 Haverstock Hill
  • 142 Regents Park Road
  • 68 Salusbury Road

JOB SUMMARY

As a Juicer at JOE & THE JUICE, your primary responsibilities are guest service and preparing food, juices, coffee, and sandwiches. You'll help ensure the bar always looks clean, welcoming, and ready for our guests. You'll report to your Store Manager, and as part of the team, your tasks may evolve alongside the store's needs.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Make every guest feel welcome and taken care of, from the moment they walk in.
  • Every juice, sandwich, and coffee we make follows a product manual, but there's one ingredient that's the same across all of them: it tastes better made with passion.
  • Keep your station and the bar spotless, because a clean bar is part of the experience too.

WHO YOU ARE

Behind every bar, on every shift, there's a Juicer who shows up with energy and makes someone's day a little brighter. That's the standard here, not one person doing it well, but all of us doing it together.

  • You show up with a "happy to be here" attitude, and you help build it, shift after shift, for the people around you.
  • You treat your teammates like family and your guests like they matter, because they do.
  • You're humble enough to learn, honest enough to be trusted.
  • You take pride in the work, even when no one's watching.
  • You're not here because a juice bar is going to change your life. Or maybe it will, most of our leaders started exactly where you're standing now. You're here because you're always looking to add one more tool to your toolbox, and this happens to be a place where you can find more than a few.

If that sounds like you, you're already one of us. Come prove it.

GOOD TO KNOW

  • How the pool works: Submit your application and we'll keep it on file. When a Juicer position opens near you, we reach out to people in the pool first.
  • No prior experience needed. Bring the right attitude and we'll teach you the rest.
  • Show up on time and looking sharp, it's part of respecting your team and your guests.
  • We'll walk you through our policies and procedures as part of onboarding, so you're never left guessing.

ABOUT JOE & THE JUICE

JOE & THE JUICE is a healthy fast-casual concept founded in Copenhagen in 2002; since then, we have grown to more than 500 locations across 20 countries and now employ more than 4,500 people worldwide. From day one, our ambition has been to prove that there should be no trade-off between taste and health.

We serve high-quality, freshly prepared juices, shakes, coffee, and sandwiches in relaxed, contemporary concept cafés that combine convenience with distinct urban atmospheres. JOE & THE JUICE goes beyond products towards the full experience around the bar, creating a consistent universe for guests and Juicers in all our locations.

We invest heavily in internal development through our Moneyball career system and a culture where most leaders, including C-suite, VPs, and directors, have started behind the bar. We continue to evolve our people-centric and sustainability agenda that is part of our Nordic heritage and our commitment to a better future.

title: Logistics Conformity Specialist and Learning Curator
description:
Description

We are looking for a motivated and structured Logistics Process Conformity Specialist to support the continuous development of our Logistics organization.In this role, you will work across process improvement, quality and compliance, training, digitalization and logistics operations, helping us build efficient, standardized and sustainable ways of working. This role is based in Galgenen, Schwyz, Switzerland.

Your Responsibilities

  • Support continuous improvement and process conformity across Logistics, including process mapping, process walks and root cause analysis.
  • Coordinate and improve training and learning processes, including training matrices, qualification tracking and Learning Management System activities.
  • Support internal and external audit preparation, follow up on corrective actions and help ensure ongoing QMS, Safety and Security compliance.
  • Create and maintain process documentation, work instructions and standards.
  • Support Logistics operations, including SAP/WMS controls, inventory counts, stock adjustments and month-end activities.
  • Prepare and monitor Logistics KPIs and Power BI reporting, ensuring accurate data and highlighting improvement opportunities.
  • Participate in system testing, digitalization and improvement projects.
  • Support customs, bonded warehouse and SOX-related processes where required.
  • Collaborate closely with Logistics, HR, Learning, Finance, IT and other key stakeholders.

What We’re Looking For

  • Education in Supply Chain, Logistics, Economics or a related field.
  • Ideally 1–3 years of relevant experience in Logistics, Supply Chain, Quality or Continuous Improvement.
  • Experience or strong interest in Lean, process improvement, quality and change management.
  • Strong analytical, organizational and problem-solving skills.
  • Structured and independent working style with a hands-on mindset.
  • Good knowledge of MS Office, particularly Excel.
  • Experience with SAP, WMS, Power BI or other reporting tools is an advantage.
  • Knowledge of Swiss customs and bonded warehouse processes is a plus.
  • Strong communication skills and confidence working with different stakeholders.
  • Advanced German and English skills.

What Will Make You Successful

You enjoy improving the way things work and combining operational understanding with a strong focus on quality, compliance and continuous improvement. You are curious, collaborative and comfortable taking ownership in a fast-changing logistics environment.

We offer you:

  • a fantastic opportunity to work in an international, fast-paced, and high-touch environment
  • a nurturing and challenging culture that is respectful of our roots and promotes intensive career development across multiple functions
  • to be part of a company that creates prestige beauty products that also advance sustainability and help contribute to a stable climate and a healthy, beautiful planet

We look forward to receiving your application.

Manager, Resource & Capacity Management, GOC

  • Process execution and operational ownership: Execute approved staffing processes across demand intake, capacity review, allocation, deployment, bench management, reporting and escalations. Translate direction into actions, owners and deadlines, ensuring accurate systems, clear handoffs and operational coverage.

Lead operational escalations, document decisions and escalate complex or unresolved issues to the Senior Manager with recommended actions.

Implement, test and document approved changes, track their impact and reinforce responsible handling of confidential employee and client information.

Skills and Experience

If this opportunity looks right for you, we are looking for candidates who have:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience in business, HR, operations, analytics, project management or a related field.
  • Approximately 5 to 7 years in resource management, staffing, workforce operations or comparable professional services, with experience owning operational processes and coordinating or coaching junior colleagues.

Our comprehensive benefits package reflects this commitment, including competitive medical, group retirement plans, vision, and dental insurance, significant paid time off, preferential partner discounts, and employee mental health awareness days.

description:
Job Title: Electronics Technician

Job Category: Engineering and Technical Support

Time Type: Full time

Minimum Clearance Required to Start: Secret

Employee Type: Regular

Percentage of Travel Required: Up to 10%

Type of Travel: Continental US

* * *

The Opportunity:

CACI is seeking an Electronics Technician and Hazardous Waste Specialist to support our prototype research and development team at Aberdeen Proving Ground, Maryland. In this dual-role position, you’ll work with engineers and technicians to build, test, and troubleshoot prototype electronics. You’ll also coordinate day-to-day hazardous waste activities for the shop, including container inspections, recordkeeping, and pickups. Your work will help move prototypes from design through test while keeping shop operations aligned with site environmental procedures.

Responsibilities:

Assemble, modify, and repair prototype electronics, including printed circuit board assemblies, cable harnesses, and electromechanical systems.

Interpret schematics, wiring diagrams, engineering drawings, and work instructions to build assemblies and verify their configuration.

Perform soldering, crimping, connector termination, and board rework using appropriate tools and electrostatic discharge controls.

Use multimeters, oscilloscopes, and bench power supplies to perform functional checks, troubleshoot faults, and document test results.

Work with engineers to resolve build and test issues. Record as-built changes, discrepancies, and rework to maintain traceability.

Maintain designated hazardous waste accumulation areas. Inspect containers and storage areas, verify labeling and segregation, and maintain inspection and inventory records in accordance with site procedures.

Coordinate waste characterization and pickups with site environmental personnel. Report leaks, spills, or inspection findings and track corrective actions through closure.

Qualifications:

Required:

High school diploma or equivalent and demonstrated hands-on experience in electronics assembly, testing, troubleshooting, or repair.

Ability to read electrical schematics and wiring diagrams and use standard electronics test equipment.

Experience with soldering, cable or harness assembly, and electrical connector termination.

Experience handling hazardous waste in a laboratory, shop, manufacturing, or industrial setting, including container labeling and recordkeeping.

Ability to complete and maintain site-required hazardous waste and safety training.

Desired:

Associate degree, technical certificate, or military technical training in electronics or a related field.

Experience supporting prototype development or low-volume electronics manufacturing.

IPC J-STD-001 or IPC/WHMA-A-620 certification, or experience working to either standard.

Experience performing hazardous waste accumulation area inspections, coordinating waste pickups, or supporting environmental audits.

-

A culture of integrity.

At CACI, we place character and innovation at the center of everything we do. As a valued team member, you’ll be part of a high-performing group dedicated to our customer’s missions and driven by a higher purpose – to ensure the safety of our nation.

CACI values the unique contributions that every employee brings to our company and our customers - every day. You’ll have the autonomy to take the time you need through a unique flexible time off benefit and have access to robust learning resources to make your ambitions a reality.

A focus on continuous growth.

Together, we will advance our nation's most critical missions, build on our lengthy track record of business success, and find opportunities to break new ground — in your career and in our legacy.


Pay Range:

There are a host of factors that can influence final salary including, but not limited to, geographic location, Federal Government contract labor categories and contract wage rates, relevant prior work experience, specific skills and competencies, education, and certifications. title: GIS Technician
description:
JOB SUMMARY

Responsible for making maps, assisting GIS application creation and manipulating data to serve a variety of purposes. Manages data entered into an enterprise GIS database and develops products (e.g., maps, datasets, summary reports) to support District projects products and programs. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

  • Reviews and analyzes data and results and develops written and verbal recommendations for continuous improvement.
  • Coordinates and consults with other workers to analyze data and use applications and tools to solve problems.
  • Provides technical/statistical information and products (e.g. graphs, reports, maps, data and document research, data management, field inspections and document control) using District applications (e.g. GIS) and software tools to meet District needs.
  • Builds and maintains effective relationship by providing support that align with organization and stakeholder goals.
  • Prepares and provides status reporting and meeting materials as required.
  • Prepares written agendas, written summaries of issues and action plans for review by supervisor and other department leaders.
  • Participates in meetings within the project groups.
  • Performs other duties of a similar nature as may be required.

MINIMUM JOB REQUIREMENTS

EDUCATION

  • Candidate must possess an associate degree, preferably in Engineering Technology, Geography/GIS, Information Systems.
  • Equivalent combination of relevant education and experience may be substituted as outlined in the Education Equivalencies Policy.

EXPERIENCE

  • Candidate must possess one (1) year of GIS related work experience.
  • Experience may include work performed during internships, co-operative education and college coursework directly related to GIS.
  • Experience in the public works/public utility, environmental/natural resources, customer service/billing industry and/or underground utility (e.g. Water, Wastewater/Sewer and/or Stormwater) industry is preferred.

OTHER REQUIREMENTS

LICENSURE AND CERTIFICATIONS

Candidate must possess a valid driver’s license with a driving record in accordance with the District’s acceptable guidelines.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES

  • Candidate must be detail-oriented, well organized and work independently or as a member of a team in a fast-paced environment.
  • Candidate must have the ability to evaluate problems or situations at hand and analyze strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions and processes in order to choose proper solutions.
  • Candidate must have the ability to learn new tools, software and languages as project needs dictate.
  • Candidate must have knowledge of Design/CAD, GIS programs, the latest version of ESRI ArcGIS desktop platform and Model Builder skills.

PHYSICAL AND MENTAL REQUIREMENTS

During the course of performing the essential functions of this position, the employee must be able to compare, copy, compute, compile, analyze, coordinate, synthesize and instruct. Ability to communicate while exhibiting strong interpersonal skills is required. Physical work will need to be performed, such as standing, sitting, walking, handling, feeling, fingering, hearing and talking. Ability to lift up to 10 lbs. on an occasional basis. Position will require visual demands of near acuity, depth perception, accommodation and color vision. The position is primarily an office position, however, the need to be in the field is required on an occasional basis. While working in the field, the employee may be exposed to extreme weather, atmospheric conditions and wet and/or humid conditions.

title: Senior Counsel, Artificial Intelligence & Data Privacy
description:
The Senior Counsel, Artificial Intelligence & Data Privacy will lead and advise on global data protection and AI governance across the global jurisdictions in which AECOM operates, ensuring compliance with international privacy laws and emerging AI regulation, mitigating legal risk and supporting responsible innovation.

The role is also the embedded legal partner to AECOM's AI Engineering teams located across Europe. It helps those teams develop and deploy AI-driven products quickly while protecting AECOM's intellectual property, its clients and the people whose data it handles, giving clear, practical answers and streamlining the legal review and compliance process.

The postholder will be the gateway and quarterback between the AI teams and the wider global AECOM legal team, and a senior, business-facing partner to leaders across the business. A cultural fit with the AI teams is essential, and a technology or product background is valued.

1. Lead product counsel embedded within AI development teams

  • Act as the embedded legal partner to the AI Engineering teams across the whole product lifecycle, managing legal design and compliance issues, and making pragmatic, risk-based calls rather than adding process.
  • Build self-service playbooks, decision guides, standard templates and pre-approved positions so that engineers and product teams can get most answers without waiting for legal review.
  • Support product launches into new markets with fast, risk-based guidance on local legal requirements, product terms and AI transparency obligations.
  • Advise on the IP position of AI development, including rights to training data, model and dataset licenses, open-weight model license terms (use restrictions and attribution), open-source software compliance, and ownership of AI-generated outputs.
  • Protect clients' confidential information and IP by setting clear rules for how client construction information may be used, including for model training and fine-tuning, and ensuring product behavior matches AECOM's contractual commitments.
  • Provide generalized legal support to the AI teams, including review & negotiation of vendor and other commercial agreements, contracts, and provide advice and counsel on general legal matters where needed.
  • Act as gateway and quarterback between the AI teams and the wider global legal team: bring in the right internal specialists, leadership at all levels, and external counsel across jurisdictions, and keep spend proportionate to the risk.
  • Guide the legal team and senior stakeholders on privacy, AI governance and regulatory developments, and give strategic advice on integrating privacy and AI compliance into product development and operations.
  • Lead and coordinate legal professionals within the AECOM legal function with full or partial responsibility for related tasks and deliverables.

2. Global privacy and AI regulatory compliance

  • Advise on global privacy laws, including GDPR and UK GDPR, US federal and state laws such as CCPA/CPRA, LGPD in Brazil, PIPEDA in Canada, the Australian and New Zealand Privacy Acts, and key Asian regimes such as Singapore's PDPA. Advise on lawful basis, DPIAs, cross-border transfers and data residency.
  • Advise on AI regulation and governance, including the EU AI Act, UK AI principles, emerging US federal and state AI rules, and emerging risk frameworks, turning them into practical requirements that teams can build into their normal way of working.
  • Contribute to the development and maintenance of the company's privacy and AI governance frameworks, policies and procedures.
  • Conduct Data Protection Impact Assessments and AI Impact Assessments for new projects and technologies, and recommend technical and organizational measures to mitigate privacy and AI-related risks.
  • Establish procedures to respond to client AI-related requests and restrictions, ensuring contractual and regulatory obligations are met promptly and effectively.
  • Track and interpret legal and regulatory developments and enforcement trends in AI, IP and data protection across AECOM's markets, and brief internal stakeholders on what matters and what needs action.
  • Represent the company in regulatory inquiries and investigations related to data privacy and AI.
  • Deliver privacy and AI governance training to employees and business units and promote a culture of privacy and responsible AI by design and default.
  • A senior, experienced, qualified lawyer, with a law degree and admission in a relevant jurisdiction.
  • Deep knowledge of GDPR, UK GDPR and US privacy laws, with experience of cross-border data transfers, and of emerging AI regulatory frameworks such as the EU AI Act and how they apply to products in practice.
  • Deep expertise in intellectual property and technology commercial work, including software, data and technology licensing, SaaS, enterprise client and vendor agreements, and open-source license compliance.
  • Hands-on experience advising on AI products, including training data rights, model licensing and AI-specific contract terms.
  • Strong drafting, negotiation and advisory skills.
  • Ability to manage complex, cross-border projects and orchestrate legal support across multiple jurisdictions, working with in-house specialists and external counsel, and to communicate effectively with senior stakeholders.
  • A track record of working at pace in fast-moving product or engineering teams, explaining legal risk clearly and pragmatically, and giving straight answers that enable delivery rather than block it. A technology or product background is valued, and a cultural fit with the AI teams is needed.
  • Experience in a large global organization, working across regions, business units and enterprise governance and compliance processes.

Preferred

  • Certifications such as CIPP/E, CIPP/US, CIPM, IAPP AIGP or other AI governance credentials.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  • Experience with patent strategy for software or machine learning inventions.
  • Familiarity with the architecture, engineering and construction (AEC) sector, including how design and construction information is owned and licensed.
  • Technical literacy in how machine learning models and LLMs are trained, fine-tuned and deployed, including the difference between hosted and self-hosted models.

  • Manage project close-out activities, including snagging, testing and commissioning follow-up, practical completion, handover documentation, and warranty management.

  • Support continuous improvement initiatives and contribute to the development of project management best practices.

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Construction Management, Architecture, Project Management, or a related discipline.

  • Proven ability to lead projects in a client-facing environment and operate autonomously within a dynamic and fast-paced organisation.
  • Strong commercial awareness and sound business acumen.
  • Excellent leadership, stakeholder engagement, and relationship management capabilities.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to make informed decisions and manage competing priorities.
  • Ability to communicate effectively at all organisational levels, from site teams to senior client leadership.
  • Excellent verbal, written, presentation, and negotiation skills.
